prov.text: The provision for loan losses of $2.4 million for the three-months ended September 30, 2026 is combined with the provision reversal for unfunded commitments of $360 thousand and reported in the net aggregate of $2.0 million under the provision for credit losses in the consolidated statements of earnings for the three-months ended September 30, 2026. The provision for loan losses of $9.0 million for the nine-months ended September 30, 2026 is combined with the provision reversal for unfunded commitments of $539 thousand and reported in the net aggregate of $8.5 million under the provision for credit losses in the consolidated statements of earnings for the nine-months ended September 30, 2026.

nonint.text: Noninterest Expense . Total noninterest expense for the three-months ended September 30, 2026 was $81.1 million, compared to $73.7 million for the same period of 2025. An important measure in determining whether a financial institution effectively manages noninterest expense is the efficiency ratio, which is calculated by dividing noninterest expense by the sum of net interest income on a tax-equivalent basis and noninterest income. Lower ratios indicate better efficiency since more income is generated with a lower noninterest expense total. Our efficiency ratio was 45.59% for the third quarter of 2026 compared to 44.74% for the same quarter in 2025.

nonop.text: Noninterest Expense . Total noninterest expense for the three-months ended September 30, 2026 was $81.1 million, compared to $73.7 million for the same period of 2025. An important measure in determining whether a financial institution effectively manages noninterest expense is the efficiency ratio, which is calculated by dividing noninterest expense by the sum of net interest income on a tax-equivalent basis and noninterest income. Lower ratios indicate better efficiency since more income is generated with a lower noninterest expense total. Our efficiency ratio was 45.59% for the third quarter of 2026 compared to 44.74% for the same quarter in 2025.

tax.text: Includes tax equivalent yield adjustment of approximately $3.6 million and $3.4 million in the third quarters of 2026 and 2025, respectively, using an effective tax rate of 21% for both periods.

Net interest income.text: Net Interest Income . Net interest income is the difference between interest income on earning assets and interest expense on liabilities incurred to fund those assets. Our earning assets consist primarily of loans and investment securities. Our liabilities to fund those assets consist primarily of noninterest-bearing and interest-bearing deposits.

Noninterest income.text: Noninterest Income . Noninterest income for the third quarter of 2026 was $35.6 million, an increase of $1.4 million, when compared to $34.3 million in the same quarter of 2025. Wealth management fee income increased to $14.5 million for the third quarter of 2026 compared to $13.0 million for the third quarter of 2025. Increases are related to new account growth and increased mineral fee income due to oil and gas prices. The market value of assets under management totaled $12.4 billion at September 30, 2026, compared to $12.1 billion at September 30, 2025. Service charges on deposits increased to $6.7 million for the third quarter of 2026 compared with $6.5 million for the third quarter of 2025, primarily driven by increases in net new accounts. Mortgage related income decreased to $4.2 million for the third quarter of 2026 compared to $4.4 million in the third quarter of 2025. Mortgage volume and margins were impacted by the spike in long term rates during the third quarter of 2026.

intro.text: Headquartered in Abilene, Texas, First Financial Bankshares, Inc. is a financial holding company that through its subsidiary, First Financial Bank, operates multiple banking regions with 79 locations in Texas, including Abilene, Acton, Albany, Aledo, Alvarado, Beaumont, Boyd, Bridgeport, Brock, Bryan, Burleson, College Station, Cisco, Cleburne, Clyde, Conroe, Cut and Shoot, Decatur, Eastland, El Campo, Fort Worth, Franklin, Fulshear, Glen Rose, Granbury, Grapevine, Hereford, Huntsville, Keller, Kingwood, Lumberton, Magnolia, Mauriceville, Merkel, Midlothian, Mineral Wells, Montgomery, Moran, New Waverly, Newton, Odessa, Orange, Palacios, Port Arthur, Ranger, Rising Star, Roby, San Angelo, Southlake, Spring, Stephenville, Sweetwater, Tomball, Trent, Trophy Club, Vidor, Waxahachie, Weatherford, Willis, and Willow Park.

s.t: Low Income Housing Tax Credit Investments - The Company has investments in an affordable housing fund that will invest in real estate projects that qualify for the federal low-income housing tax credit ("LIHTC") program designed to promote private development of low income housing.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Debt securities
lines.why: Bonds held for sale or to maturity: financial.

lines.name: Loans, net of the allowance
lines.why: Lending is a bank's business: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Deposits
lines.why: Customers' money a bank holds is its business: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
